l: the yearly season of the rites of Ceres, The Amores, or Amours
s: An annual season of Ceres's rites arrives, requiring the speaker's mistress to remain separated from him throughout.
Cretans are a nation proud of nurturing Jove as a child and presented as witnesses that Ceres was not devoid of love.
is_a hunter [skilled and accurate] Iasius was seen by Ceres at the foot of Cretan Ida piercing the backs of wild beasts with an unerring hand. Ceres desired him, and Love overcame her Shame.
is_a lawgiver Minos, called law-giving, wished for many fruitful years like the one in which Crete prospered. He also wished that Ceres's love would last.

l: Ceres's daughter, The Amores, or Amours
s: Ceres's daughter is found again by Ceres and rules realms ranked only below Juno's.
is_fertile fertile [during its fruitful year] Crete alone remained fertile when Ceres lingered in the woods with Iasius. Ida grew white with corn, and even the wild boar cropped ears in the woods.
Single-blessedness is a condition the speaker endures during Ceres's rites, which he argues would have saddened Ceres.

struggles_with Love [for control of the speaker's heart] Hatred contends with Love for control of the speaker's heart. The speaker wishes to hate if he can, because of the mistress's conduct, but cannot make Hatred overcome Love.

l: ELEGY XI, The Amores, or Amours
s: is_a elegy ELEGY XI presents the speaker's confession that he cannot help loving his mistress despite her faults. It recounts his humiliation and jealousy, then ends with his admission that he will be forced to love her even if he refuses.

are_attracted_to mistress (Corinna) [because of her fame] The speaker fears that many rivals have been created because his poems made Corinna famous. They are able to approach her through the fame and access provided by his verses.

harms love [by believing poetic praise of the mistress] The credulity of others has harmed the speaker because they believed the praise given to his mistress. He says that Corinna should have been regarded as falsely praised, as poets are not usually accepted as reliable witnesses.

l: the speaker's wife, The Amores, or Amours
s: is_born_in Falisci The speaker's wife was born at Falisci, a place fruitful in apples. Her birthplace gives the speaker a reason to visit the festival of Juno there.
is_fruitful_in apples Falisci is described as fruitful in apples and as a place whose walls were conquered by Camillus. The festival of Juno is celebrated there.

l: the Falisci people, The Amores, or Amours
s: The Falisci people observe the rites of Juno. Halesus taught them those rites, and they take part in the festival's procession and offerings.

l: the festival of Juno, The Amores, or Amours
s: The chaste festival of Juno is prepared by priestesses, with distinguished games and a country heifer; a procession of victims, road-sweeping youths and girls, vessel-bearers, and silent people unfolds.

l: the sacred grove, The Amores, or Amours
s: An ancient sacred grove, shaded by countless trees, reveals a divinity through its appearance.

l: the altar, The Amores, or Amours
s: An altar in the grove, made without skill by ancient hands, receives the prayers and votive incense of the pious.

l: the yearly procession, The Amores, or Amours
s: The yearly procession, Argive and resplendent, begins at a pipe’s signal, proceeds along covered paths in silence, led by Juno’s priestesses with sacrificial animals.

l: the priestesses of Juno, The Amores, or Amours
s: are_followed_by Juno The priestesses prepare Juno's chaste festival and lead the procession. Juno follows after them.
Halesus, an exile fleeing his crime and his father’s wealth, wanders over land and sea, then prospers by erecting lofty walls and teaching his Falisci the rites of Juno.

l: the rites of Juno, The Amores, or Amours
s: are_taught_to the Falisci people [by Halesus] The rites of Juno were taught to the Falisci by Halesus. The speaker prays that they may always be propitious to him and to Juno's own people.

l: concealment of infidelity, The Amores, or Amours
s: is_requested_by mistress [from the speaker] Concealment of infidelity is presented as preferable to confession or openly displaying what happens in secret. The speaker promises not to investigate what the mistress hides and says he will treat even an apparent accusation as false. If he sees her guilt, he asks her to deny what his eyes have witnessed.

l: the public, The Amores, or Amours
s: The public is portrayed as malicious; the mistress, deceived by concealment, is urged to avoid it through modest appearance and professions of chastity.
Reputation is endangered by confessed sexual wrongdoing and consulted by an unfaithful mistress; it is preserved through concealment or imitation of chastity.

l: sexual encounter, The Amores, or Amours
s: A secret sexual encounter in a chamber involves a strumpet; participants undress, touch, kiss, speak passionately, move the bed, then leave its signs and behaviors behind.
Lyæus, a horned deity, wields a potent thyrsus, striking the poet and driving him toward a broader, mighty course.
